mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate over the past month indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance, which reduces the cost of capital and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year CPI inflation rate exceeds 3.5%, it signals persistent inflationary pressures that prompt the Federal Reserve to maintain a restrictive monetary policy, causing a temporary sell-off in equities over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 3.5%, the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 40% of such instances (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) signals strong consumer demand and confidence, which accelerates corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both increase by >0.5% MoM
failure_condition: The average 20-day return is not significantly positive (p>0.05) when PAYEMS and HOUST both increase by >0.5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle economic expansions (defined by strong GDP growth and high housing starts), the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to profit-taking and rising interest rate expectations, leading to negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 60-day return is not significantly negative (p>0.05) in periods classified as late-cycle expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate signals a tightening labor market, which typically precedes stronger consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE declines (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100.0 (index 2017=100), it signals a contraction in manufacturing and supply chain disruptions, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to recession fears.
failure_condition: When INDPRO falls below 100.0, the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer spending, which drives corporate revenue growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when RSAFS increases (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 4.5% per annum, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and dampens equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 45% of instances (p>0.05).
